passage: After the meeting where the regional head announced that the delayed shipment was "Chinmay's oversight", Chinmay sat at his desk staring at nothing. The delay had been a warehouse fault, and he had emailed about it twice. Eshaan, two desks away, stayed back after everyone left and slid a printout onto his desk: the forwarded warnings, highlighted. "I sent the same thing to the regional head. Said I'd seen it myself." "They'll notice you," Chinmay said. "Let them." Chinmay swallowed. Next morning he told the head that any follow-up should come to him first, not Eshaan, since he had been the one on the account. At lunch he set a tiffin box on Eshaan's desk. "I owe you more than this." Eshaan grinned. "Then remember it."

qa.q: What was highlighted on the printout Eshaan gave Chinmay?
How did Chinmay feel about Eshaan's support, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Chinmay was moved and grateful: he swallowed, tried to shield Eshaan by asking that follow-up come to him first, and said he owed more than a tiffin box.

qa.q: How did Chinmay try to protect Eshaan and honour the debt?
qa.a: He asked the head to send any follow-up to him first and set a tiffin box on Eshaan's desk, saying he owed more than that.

qa.q: How might Eshaan see the risk taken?
qa.a: Eshaan seems aware of being noticed and says "Let them", which suggests standing up for fairness mattered more than staying safe.

grounding: A coworker stands by Chinmay after an unfair blame; he thanks them, tries to shield them from consequences and remembers the debt.
